note: PACK-006 preserve OCI platform: one index, one manifest per platform, each descriptor carrying the platform it was built for - which is the only thing a runtime uses to choose between them, so it is asserted rather than copied hopefully. src/package/oci.zig buildMulti gives each request its own configuration and layers, so the manifests genuinely differ, and the shared index is the only document tying them together; the arm64 entry records its variant, because a runtime that needs v8 will not choose an entry without it. Every descriptor in the multi-platform layout validates against its blob, so a platform is never recorded beside a wrong image. The test covers three targets (linux/x86_64, linux/aarch64/v8, windows/x86_64), asserts each index entry's os and architecture, and refuses a request with an empty os or architecture before any document is built, because a descriptor with an empty platform is an image a runtime cannot choose. Fault proof: recording the first platform for every manifest - a runtime choosing the wrong image for two of three targets - makes the case fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
